text:
Marina: perf-bot just flagged a regression in CI for the nightly longctx memory test — OOMs and sustained RSS growth after yesterday's release. any eyes? :eyes:
perf-bot: [automated] test=kv-mem-longctx runner=gpu-32 failure_type=OOM peak_rss=45.2GB step=312 build_ref=refs/heads/main@{#8342}
Kai: ugh, saw the alert. which change landed in 8342?
Marina: looks like a batch/route refactor and a small tweak to the kernel selection thresholds by Lucas (pushed ~18:30 PT). Also an eviction-window tweak landed in the same PR.
Lucas: yup, that was my PR. I adjusted routing so for seq_len > 1024 we prefer the fp16 kernel path and I tightened the eviction window to reduce cache churn under small prompts. didn't expect this to blow up memory for long sequences.
Anya: could be slab packing interaction. When eviction threshold changes you can get more fragmentation and slab churn for large KV entries. I can repro locally with the longctx harness.
Marina: repro steps please — want to bisect quickly before rolling out a revert.
Anya: repro script below (run on a 48GB GPU):
```bash
# reproduce longctx leak-ish behavior
python infra/longctx_repro.py --model redwood-30b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --steps 400 --kv-cache enabled
# watch top and /proc/`pid`/smaps or use pmap
```
Anya: reproduces consistently here — RSS climbs steadily until OOM around step 300-330. grabbing jemalloc stats now.
Marina: start a git bisect? we need to narrow to a single commit within the merge.
Kai: starting bisect across commits 8338..8346, will run the longctx job on each commit in the bisection. I'll parallelize across two runners.
Lucas: quick note — the kernel-router change touched kernel_selector.cc and cache_eviction.cc in the same PR. If bisect points to my commit I'll add more instrumentation to kernel selection and slab accounting.
Anya: here's a short log excerpt around the crash: 
```
[2026-03-18T02:12:41Z] kv_cache: allocated slab=0x7f3a2e size=8192 seq_entries=512
[2026-03-18T02:12:44Z] slab-alloc: split->resident=120MB free_frag=34%
[2026-03-18T02:13:02Z] kernel-router: selected fp16_path for seq_len=2048 (latency_win=7)
[2026-03-18T02:13:18Z] OOM: out of memory allocating 16384 bytes
```
Anya: jemalloc stats show arena fragmentation rising to ~40% before the OOM.
Kai: bisect progress: good=8338 bad=8346 midpoint=8342 (the merge commit). testing 8342 now.
Marina: if midpoint is the merge itself we need to try the individual commits inside the merge, because it's a stacked change.
Kai: drilled down — bad when testing commit 8344, good at 8343. 8344 is the kernel routing heuristic tweak.
Lucas: that pins it to my change. I'll revert 8344 on canary and re-run the CI longctx to confirm.
Marina: please do a canary rollback and post results. prefer automated rollback if possible.
deploy-bot: rollback request accepted for canary group. initiating rollback of refs/heads/main@{#8344}...
deploy-bot: rollback complete on canary (2/2 hosts), health checks pass.
Kai: re-ran the nightly longctx once canary rolled back — no OOM, peak_rss stabilized ~18GB, test passed.
Anya: local confirmed: applying revert to 8344 removes the steady RSS climb. Also verified slab fragmentation stays <12%.
Lucas: opening PR now: revert(8344) + instrumentation (kernel selection histograms, slab age buckets, jemalloc staging flags). I'll include a small canary that toggles the fp16 prefer flag off for seq_len>1024.
Marina: thanks. next steps: 1) ship revert asap, 2) add telemetry to kernel selection and cache slabs, 3) run extended longctx stress in CI gate (48h) before reintroducing heuristic. also add an automated perf test that exercises seq_len distribution skew (long tails).
Lucas: ack — will include all instrumentation and a perf test in the revert PR.
Marina: good catch everyone. once PR is open drop link here and I'll approve the revert and schedule a hotfix release. :+1:
Lucas: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8349 (revert + instrumentation)
Marina: approving and merging into hotfix branch. after hotfix we can run a small canary rollout and then re-evaluate with the added metrics.
Anya: I'll add a flamegraph capture step to the longctx job so we can see where allocations spike in the kernel path.
Marina: perfect — let's close after the hotfix stabilizes. thanks all.
